records.name: Practice Yoga Co-op
records.summary: A worker-owned yoga co-op in Philadelphia where the teachers run classes, events and workshops together. Drop-in classes are by donation, and mats and props are free to use.
records.what_you_do: Drop in to a class without signing up and pay what you choose, with a suggested minimum of $15. Mats and props are free. Ellen's Iyengar classes cost more and are priced separately.

schedule.text: Vinyasa, align and flow, embodied flow, restorative and Iyengar classes run through the week. Ellen's Monday and Thursday 6 pm Iyengar classes are labeled beginner friendly, and her Level II classes meet Tuesday evening and Saturday morning. Zoom classes need a separate sign up at practiceyogastudio.com, and the schedule page shows the current week.

cost.text: Most drop-in classes are by donation with a suggested minimum of $15, and no one is turned away for lack of funds. Ellen's Iyengar classes are priced separately: $25 a drop-in, or $20 a class with a 10-class card that expires after six months.

requirements.gear: Mats and props are provided free, so you do not need your own.

first_step.how: Show up to an in-person drop-in class with no sign up needed. For a beginner class, try Ellen's Monday or Thursday 6 pm Iyengar class, which is $25 a drop-in or $20 a class with a 10-class card.
first_step.basis: The team page labels Ellen's Monday and Thursday 6 pm Iyengar classes as beginner friendly, and the co-op says in-person drop-ins need no advance sign up. It does not describe a newcomer program or orientation.
first_step.what_to_expect: No sign up is needed for in-person drop-in classes. You pay what you choose, with a suggested $15 minimum, and mats and props are free. Ellen's Iyengar classes run 75 to 90 minutes and are priced separately from the donation classes.
first_visit_tips: Mats and props are free, so you do not need to bring your own.
Ellen's Iyengar classes are not donation based, so check the price before you go.
Zoom classes need their own sign up at practiceyogastudio.com.
The site does not say where the door is or how to get there, so call (215) 755-3268 or email info@practiceyogacoop.com before your first visit.

records.notes: Contact page lists practiceyoga1@gmail.com as its contact email. Kept info@ from tier 1 because the home page gives it, and both are published on the site. The schedule page lists the teachers but no timetable, so the Iyengar times come from the team page. The October 2026 class listings on the home page are dated events, so they count only toward last_sign_of_life and are not in the schedule text. The tier 1 address came from a 2024 listing; the group's contact page now confirms 804 S 4th St.

records.name: Queer Run
records.summary: A free run club for LGBTQIA+ runners in Philadelphia, run as a nonprofit. Runners of all paces meet for weekly runs in Center City and Manayunk.
records.what_you_do: Run three or four miles with other queer runners at your own pace, starting from a meeting point on a weekly run night.

schedule.text: Weekly runs: Mondays at 7 pm from the center of Rittenhouse Square (3 miles), Wednesdays at 6 pm from Philadelphia Runner in Manayunk (3 miles), and Thursdays at 6 am from the southwest corner of Love Park (4 miles). Runs stop halfway for stretching and conversation, and they go on year round except in severe weather, when cancellations are posted on the site.

cost.text: Free. Donations are optional and go through the group's support page.

first_step.how: Go to the meeting spot for one weekly run, such as Monday at 7 pm at the center of Rittenhouse Square. You can email contact@queerrun.net with questions before you go.
first_step.basis: The site says all runners are welcome whatever their background or experience, runs are open to all paces, and each run has a named meeting spot and time.
first_step.what_to_expect: Runs are free and go on year round except in severe weather. Each run is 3 or 4 miles at your own pace, with a stop halfway for stretching and conversation. Runners are not compared with one another, and the group puts care for each other first.
first_visit_tips: Check the site for cancellations before you go, since runs are cancelled in severe weather and the cancellations are posted on the site.
Meet at the spot listed for your run: the center of Rittenhouse Square, Philadelphia Runner in Manayunk, or the southwest corner of Love Park.
The site does not say what to bring or wear, so email contact@queerrun.net if you are unsure.

records.notes: Next run dates on the site (the 5th, 7th and 8th of October) carry no year, so no 2026 date is recorded and status stays probably_active. The calendar on the site is an image that could not be read. The contact name Josh Fernandez comes from IRS and NCCS data in tier 1, not from the group's own site; the owner should decide whether to publish it. The site also invites allies, not only queer runners.

records.name: Queerobics West Philly
records.summary: A pop-up dance class and performance project led by queer and trans dance artists, disabled people and chronically ill community members. Low-impact and seated versions are offered.
records.what_you_do: Join a pop-up class in outdoor park and court settings, with dance captains offering low-impact and seated options. Masks are required.

schedule.text: Pop-up classes with no fixed weekly schedule. Dates are posted one class at a time on the Next Class page.

locations.label: Pop-up park or court (changes by class)

cost.text: Suggested donation of $10 to $15 per class. No one is turned away for lack of funds. Donations go through the group's fundraising page or its Ko-fi page.

requirements.gear: A mask is required, and the group has a limited supply to share. Wear comfortable athletic clothes.

access.notes: The Next Class page lists a barrier-free entrance and space, an accessible restroom, bench seating with demonstrations from a seat, and water. Classes are held on grass. Classes are pop-ups, so check the Next Class page for each class's location.

first_step.how: Read the Next Class page on queerobics.com for the date and park, then email queerobics@gmail.com to ask how to sign up before you come.
first_step.basis: Open to the public, with seated and low-impact options and an email contact. The Next Class page does not say beginners are welcome and does not spell out how to register.
first_step.what_to_expect: The class is an accessibility-centered dance and movement class held outdoors in parks or on courts. Dance captains show moves live beside the lead instructor and offer low-impact and seated options. Masks are required, and the suggested donation is $10 to $15, with no one turned away for lack of funds.
first_visit_tips: Bring a mask if you can, because the group has only a limited supply.
Wear comfortable athletic clothes, like the instructors in the group's flyers.
Water is available at class.
Check the Next Class page for the location before you go, since each class is a pop-up.

records.notes: The home page says to register for the next class through the fundraising page, but the Next Class page lists no registration steps. The record says to email to ask, and sign_up_needed is true; confirm before publishing. The dated class on the Next Class page (October 10, 2026) is recorded only through last_sign_of_life and its URL, not in schedule text. Partners named on the site (FringeArts, Painted Bride, cinéSPEAK, Cannonball Festival, Art-Reach) are venues or festivals with no URLs captured, so they are not listed as leads.

records.name: Quintessence Theatre Group
records.summary: A theatre company in residence at the Sedgwick Theater in Mt. Airy. It stages a season of plays and runs classes, student matinees and a summer camp.
records.what_you_do: Buy tickets to a season show, take an adult workshop, or bring a student group. Volunteers usher, hand out flyers at local businesses, prepare mailings, and help build sets and costumes.

schedule.text: A season of plays runs each year (Season XVII is the current one). The Shakespeare Gym workshop for working actors meets Sundays from 7 to 9:30 pm in sessions with set dates, and the education pages list other workshops.

cost.text: Tickets are about $30 to $75, with previews at the low end and opening nights at the high end. Youth 18 and under pay $30 to $35, seniors get $5 off full price, active military pay $25 to $30, and a limited number of $10 rush tickets go on sale in person one hour before curtain.

access.notes: The site calls the theater accessible and has an accessible restroom in the lobby. You can ask for seating accommodations when you buy tickets. Some performances have open captioning, but the site does not say which ones. To confirm the entrance and seating, email the box office. SEPTA Bus 23 stops at Mount Pleasant Avenue, and the page names Allen Lane and Sedgwick stations on the Chestnut Hill rail lines nearby.

first_step.how: Buy a ticket to a Season XVII show, or email volunteer@quintessencetheatre.org to ask about ushering.
first_step.basis: Shows are open to anyone with a ticket, and the site has an email sign up for volunteers. The adult workshop listed is aimed at working actors and does not say beginners are welcome.
first_step.what_to_expect: Shows are staged at the Sedgwick Theater on Germantown Avenue, and you can buy tickets in advance or try for a limited $10 rush ticket in person about an hour before curtain. If you usher, you get a free ticket to the show you work and a free concessions item, with no alcohol.
first_visit_tips: Park in the free lot directly across from the theater, or use the unmetered street spaces on Germantown Avenue, which have a 2-hour limit.
Take SEPTA Bus 23 to Mount Pleasant Avenue. The site warns that the trip from Center City takes a long time, so allow extra time.
Ask for seating accommodations when you buy tickets, in person or online.
Volunteers must be 18 or older, or 15 to 17 with a guardian. Email volunteer@quintessencetheatre.org with your availability and interests.

records.notes: Show dates are not written in the page text (only a banner filename hints at them), so no dated evidence is recorded and status stays probably_active. The accessibility page says the theater is accessible but does not say whether the entrance is step-free, so wheelchair is yes on the site's word; a reviewer may want to confirm. The site lists two Germantown Avenue addresses: 7137 is the theater and 7135 is the administrative office. The record uses the theater. Ticket prices change by show, so the cost text gives ranges.

records.name: RAIR Inc.
records.summary: An arts organization at 7333 Milnor Street in the Northeast that runs an artist residency, public tours and community events, including a yearly event called Trash Bash.
records.what_you_do: Book a tour of the facility, volunteer through the site's Volunteer section, or come to the yearly Trash Bash party, a ticketed evening of food, drinks and a silent auction of donated art.

schedule.text: Tours are offered in person or online, typically at least once a month, and upcoming dates are posted on the tours page and on Instagram. The yearly Trash Bash party is a ticketed evening event.

cost.text: Tour prices are not listed on the tours page. Recent Trash Bash tickets cost about $90 to $160, depending on the ticket type.

access.notes: Access needs are handled case by case. Email the creative director at billy@rairphilly.org before a visit. The tours page also offers a pre-recorded tour on YouTube for people who cannot attend a live one.

first_step.how: Book a tour through the links on the Tours page of rairphilly.org, or email info@rairphilly.org to ask about the next tour or community event.
first_step.basis: Tours and the yearly party are open to the public and booked through clear links, and the Volunteer page invites sign ups. The site does not describe a beginner program.
first_step.what_to_expect: Tours run in person or online, typically at least once a month. A virtual tour lasts about an hour and ends with time for questions, and you get the Zoom link the Friday before. In-person tours are limited in size, so book ahead.
first_visit_tips: Book a space through the Ticketleap links on the Tours page, and email info@rairphilly.org with questions.
For a virtual tour, watch for the Zoom link, which comes the Friday before.
If you cannot attend live, a pre-recorded tour is on YouTube.
For access needs, email billy@rairphilly.org before you come.

records.notes: The Trash Bash page gives a Wednesday in November with a 5:30 to 9:30 pm evening, but no year sits beside the date. The page title says 2026, so last_sign_of_life uses 2026 only and the November date is kept out of the record. The volunteer page says to sign up, but no form or roles appear in the page text. Tour prices are not on the tours page. The contact name Fern Gookin comes from IRS and NCCS data in tier 1, while the group's site names Billy Dufala as creative director; the owner should decide which name to publish.

records.name: Realist Artists League
records.summary: An art studio in the Globe Dye Works building on Worth Street, focused on painting and drawing from life, with a figure and portrait focus.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for an open studio session to draw or paint from a live model, or take one of the studio's specialized classes.

schedule.text: Open studio runs Saturdays and Sundays, 9 am to 4 pm, with a live model in long pose figure and portrait sessions. Ongoing figure and still life classes meet on weekdays in multi-week terms: figure painting on Mondays and Thursdays, and still life on Tuesdays, both during the day.

cost.text: Open studio is $25 for one day or $40 for both days, and card payments add a fee. Classes are sold by multi-week term, starting at about $900, and figure painting also offers a $100 drop-in day.

requirements.gear: Bring your own art materials; the studio provides easels and tables.

first_step.how: Contact the studio before your first open studio day (a Saturday or Sunday, 9 am to 4 pm) to get parking and entry details, then pay $25 for the day.
first_step.basis: Open studio is open to artists who contact the studio first. The page calls the space judgment-free but does not say beginners are welcome. The studio's classes say all experience levels are welcome.
first_step.what_to_expect: Open studio is a full day, 9 am to 4 pm, built around a six-hour pose with a live model. You bring your own art materials, and the studio provides easels and tables. One day costs $25, or $40 for both weekend days.
first_visit_tips: Check the open studio page for closed weekends before you come, since some Saturdays are closed.
Cash, check or Zelle avoid the card fee that applies to credit card payments.
Bring your own art materials; the studio provides easels and tables.

records.notes: Email conflict: the open studio page shows studio@realistartleague.com, but its link points to realistartleague@gmail.com. The tier 1 address is kept; confirm before publishing. The open studio page does not say whether sessions are drop in or reserved, so the record says to contact the studio first. Whether models are clothed is not stated, so it is not recorded. Dated items on the site (closed weekends, term dates) carry no year and are left out. The pages say nothing about stairs or wheelchair access.

records.name: Recreation Advisory Councils
records.summary: Lets anyone become a voting member of their local rec center's advisory council just by attending one meeting and signing in, with elected officer roles for more involved members.
records.what_you_do: Help your rec center decide which programs to offer, raise money for supplies and equipment, plan events, and help keep the center clean.

schedule.text: Each rec center has its own council, and the councils are expected to meet monthly at the center. The 2016 manual asks for the same time and place each month, so ask your rec center staff for the next date.

cost.text: Joining and voting cost nothing, since the 2016 manual bars fees for membership and voting rights.

first_step.how: Attend one meeting of your rec center's council and sign the sign-in sheet so your name is on it. Ask the rec center staff for the next meeting date, since the city page does not list one.
first_step.basis: The city says anyone can join by attending one meeting and signing in, and the 2016 manual says meetings are open to the public. The city page gives no meeting dates, so you need to ask your rec center.
first_step.what_to_expect: Meetings are open to the public and are held at the rec center, with the date, time and place posted there at least five days ahead, according to the city's 2016 manual. Members can vote in council elections and help plan programs and events, and to vote or hold office you must be a registered volunteer or adult participant at the center, or the parent of a registered child there. Officer posts (president, vice president, treasurer and secretary) require being 18 and having attended 70 percent of meetings in the election cycle, and the 2016 manual also requires a criminal background check and child abuse clearance for officers.
first_visit_tips: Ask the staff at your rec center for the next meeting date and time, since the city page does not list them.
Look for the meeting notice posted in the rec center, which must go up at least five days before each meeting.
To vote or hold office later, register as a volunteer or adult participant at the center, or as the parent of a registered child there.
Officers must pass a criminal background check and child abuse clearance under the 2016 manual, so plan ahead if you want that role.

records.notes: Each council is separate, so this record describes the program as a whole. The current city page says anyone can join after one meeting, but it lists no meeting dates and no background check rule. Meeting frequency, the posting rule and the officer background check come from the city's Advisory Council Manual, revised October 2016, the newest manual found; confirm current rules with the rec center. Status and last_sign_of_life 2024-02 were carried from tier 1: the city page now shows no dates, and 2024-02 is 32 months old, which the status rules would call dormant. The owner should check whether probably_active stands.

The city's Advisory Council Manual (revised October 2016) could not be read by WebFetch, so it was read from the saved copy with the Read tool; that read is not counted as a fetch. Partner names on the Queerobics and RAIR sites (FringeArts, Painted Bride, cinéSPEAK, Cannonball Festival, Art-Reach, Atelier FAS Gallery) have no URLs captured, so they are not listed as leads.
